answer: Peer-reviewed identity graphs require each edge to be mutual with a distinct already-earning endorser, so trust equals the minimum cut over reciprocal links, not degree. Each attempt costs a per-identity bond, an attestation fee, and a rate-capped maturation delay. A fake ring fails because its internal edges never reach an independent earner: the plume of linked addresses remains isolated, rewards flow back along one river to the ring's origin, and no identity reaches the quorum zenith required to vote.
